items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: Sharky had called me like five months in advance and he said, Bob, would you like to make a road tour with me? I said, well, sure.

ctx.x: You can meet some real problems. Well, anyhow, there's a lot of bands that we talked about and we'd mentioned the leader. But for example, we never did talk about really who was in Sharky's band and too much of what you did with him.

Well, at the time, I was with the Sharky group. Sharky had called me like five months in advance and he said, Bob, would you like to make a road tour with me? I said, well, sure. But I said, when are you planning on leaving? And he said, oh, I'm about six months from now. I said, well, Sharky, why don't you call me about two months in advance? And then I could more officially give you an answer. You know, I mean, I don't like to plan anything six months in advance. That's pretty far away. So he says, okay. So he…
Did you say who the clarinet player was? Oh, uh... Start at the top. The high note.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: And that's what I enjoyed the year working with Sharky's Dixieland band, with the old Sharky's Kings of Dixieland.

ctx.x: And he knows tunes like, I'll Be a Friend with Pleasure. One day I just wanted to bug him and I asked him for that. He knew it.

What I like about Connie Jones is not only his marvelous playing, but like you just mentioned, he plays a lot of tunes, good old Dixieland tunes, that a lot of the other Dixieland bands don't play. Oh yeah. And that's what I enjoyed the year working with Sharky's Dixieland band, with the old Sharky's Kings of Dixieland. I enjoyed that year with Sharky because Sharky played a lot of good old Dixieland tunes that I had not played with any of the other groups. Even when I was with Al Hurd or the late George Arrod,…
I remember when he had that examination and everything. It just sounded hopeless from what Johnny Wiggs told me. Johnny I think was the one who told me about it. It was a shock.
